explainBack.question: Why can two teams asking the Data agent the same question get different polished dashboards, and why does neither dashboard prove itself right?
explainBack.answer: Each answer is produced downstream of three constraints the interface hides: which sources administrators connected, which tables, rows and columns that account's permissions expose, and which metric definition converts records into a number. If one team defines active customers as weekly logins and another as monthly buyers, or one account lacks a region's rows, the totals diverge before rendering. The dashboard's polish reflects presentation, not the correctness of any upstream link, and no external accuracy benchmark exists to certify the agent's reliability.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: An accurate answer must cite the source-definition-permission chain (P007), the diverging active-customer definitions and missing-region permission effect (P008), and ideally the absent external benchmark (P005).
explainBack.assessment: The artifact fully supports this causal answer in ordinary language; all necessary steps are present and correctly ordered, so the explain-back succeeds.

unseenTransfer.scenario: An HR partner asks the Data agent for 'quarterly attrition' the night before a board meeting. Contractors are tracked in a separate staffing tool that was never connected, the partner's account only has permissions for two of three regions, and the company has never settled whether attrition counts voluntary leavers only or all departures.
unseenTransfer.question: Using the article's mechanism, what should the HR partner check before putting the agent's attrition figure in front of the board, and why?
unseenTransfer.answer: Apply the chain: first the source — the staffing tool is unconnected, so contractor departures are invisible to the agent regardless of prompt quality; second the permissions — the missing third region silently lowers headcount and departure totals; third the definition — voluntary-only versus all-departures produces different rates that both render as polished dashboards. The partner should name the connected source and date, state which attrition definition was applied, compare the figure against the trusted HR report, and stop at any discrepancy rather than choosing the convenient number, since no external benchmark certifies the agent's accuracy.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: Correct transfer requires mapping all three constraints from P007 and P008 to the new HR facts, plus the P009 comparison routine and P005 benchmark caveat.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism transfers cleanly to this unseen scenario without needing any concept the article omits; the transfer succeeds.
